context:
Goal: a lane can fix its own commit without opening a replacement PR.
Problem (rule): the auto-mode classifier refuses a lease push to a lane's own branch. Each refusal costs a replacement PR. Only you can change auto-mode permissions.
Based on (measured): main's notes record 9 refusals and 8 replacement PRs, Nov 2 to 4, all claude-settings lanes. Causes: 5 red-run trailer amends, 1 merge-commit repair, 1 rebase, 1 subject fix, 1 unstated. Time lost per replacement: 6 min to 4 h 13 min, most 6 to 26 min.
Based on (read): in 5 of 9, the red-run check's remedy (lint/check_red_run.py) names a bare `git push --force-with-lease`, which the force-push guard denies; the guard's own remedy names `--force-with-lease --force-if-includes`. The two remedies disagree.
Based on (read): an allow rule matches exact text only, and cannot tell a lane's own branch from another lane's, archive/* or merge-lock/*; the guard does not check branch owner either. Whether an allow rule beats the classifier is documented, not measured.
Departs from: main (the classifier refuses lease pushes) — a adds a Bash allow rule; c adds an auto-mode prose allow entry; d changes the red-run check's remedy so no force push is needed.

One Opus agent reviewed this with no recommendation, as you asked (17:44 CST); this item makes none.

lastAnswer.note: Send an opus agent to review these options unbiased.

options.gain: No replacement PR when the exact form is used.
options.how: Allow `git push --force-with-lease=<branch>:<sha>` off the default branch.
options.label: Bash allow rule for the lease push (Goes against your ruling: a repo changes to fit a shared tool, never the tool to fit a repo)
options.lose: No logged command used that form; the rule cannot tell a lane's own branch from another lane's, archive/* or merge-lock/*; whether it beats the classifier is unmeasured.

options.label: Leave it as it is
options.lose: About 8 replacement PRs in 3 days, most 6 to 26 min each.

options.gain: The classifier keeps judging each push, with your words as its guide.
options.how: An autoMode.allow entry in decision auto-mode-owner-acts, like Archived Branch Delete: a lease push to a branch this session pushed earlier, never default, archive/, roadmap or merge-lock. The classifier still judges.
options.label: Auto-mode prose allow entry (Goes against your ruling: a repo changes to fit a shared tool, never the tool to fit a repo)
options.lose: Whether it lets a lease push through is unknown until tried.

options.gain: Removes 5 of the 9 refusals with no widening; the two remedies stop disagreeing.
options.how: The red-run check's remedy points at a route with no force push, or the trailer is checked before the first push.
options.label: Remove the cause in the red-run check
options.lose: Rebases and merge-commit repairs still meet the refusal.

ref: one Opus agent's unbiased review via the coordinator, 2026-11-04 17:54 CST; docs/debts/notes.md classifier-refuses-lease-push; lint/check_red_run.py
short: Lease push refusals: allow, leave, or fix cause?
title: Lease pushes: auto mode refuses a lane's fix to its own branch. Allow it, leave it, or remove the cause?
